3. Homepage Only — Header/Nav Element Not Visible

Critical1 page · all 4 viewports
CriticalNAVHomepage only
On the homepage, header/nav element is completely absent from the visible DOM at all desktop widths
Playwright's page.locator('header, nav').first().isVisible() returns false on https://uof.rt.gw/ at all 4 desktop viewports (1280, 1366, 1440, 1920px). This is distinct from the general hamburger issue — on every other page the nav element exists and is visible (as a collapsed hamburger). On the homepage, the nav element itself is not rendered visibly. This is likely a homepage-specific hero template or CSS rule that hides or overlaps the header.
URL: https://uof.rt.gw/ only Viewports: 1280×800, 1366×768, 1440×900, 1920×1080 Fix: Check homepage template for header z-index, display, or visibility override that hides the nav element
Affected URL (1)
https://uof.rt.gw/
https://uof.rt.gw/ — All desktop viewports 1280–1920px

4. Nav Collapses to Hamburger at All Desktop Widths

Critical116 pages · 1280 / 1366 / 1440 / 1920px
CriticalNAV116 pages × 4 viewports
The hamburger toggle ≡ is shown at 1280, 1366, 1440 and 1920×1080 — the nav never renders as a full bar on any tested desktop screen
v2 of this report incorrectly stated only 1280px and 1366px. The data confirms the hamburger is visible at all four desktop viewports: 1280×800, 1366×768, 1440×900, and 1920×1080. This means a 27-inch 1080p monitor shows a hamburger instead of a navigation bar. The CSS @media nav-collapse breakpoint either has no lower bound, or is set so high that no tested viewport escapes it.
Viewports: 1280×800, 1366×768, 1440×900, 1920×1080 — every desktop size tested Selector: button[aria-label*="menu"] visible on all 116 live pages Fix: Remove or significantly lower the max-width breakpoint that triggers mobile nav
https://uof.rt.gw/about/ — 1280×800 shown — same at 1366, 1440, 1920px

5. Broken Images — Asset Not Migrated

Critical23 pages
CriticalBROKEN_IMG23 pages
img.naturalWidth === 0 after page load — image source returns error response
v2 of this report incorrectly listed this as Warning. The test data marks "Broken image detected" as critical severity (checks.ts line 171). These are not styling issues — the image asset itself fails to load, leaving empty grey boxes visible to users. Separate from missing alt text (which is Warning). Fix: audit the WordPress media library and CDN paths post-migration.
Severity: Critical (naturalWidth=0 after networkidle)Fix: Restore missing assets or update src paths in media library

6. Testimonial Circle Image Overflows Container

Warning3 pages
WarningBROKEN_IMG — Layout3 pages
img.findlay-testimonial__image--circle bleeds beyond its parent wrapper
This issue was missing from v2 of this report. Three pages use a circular testimonial image component. The image element's bounding rect exceeds its parent container width at 1280, 1366, and 1440px. The circle visually bleeds into adjacent content. Not detected at 1920px.
Selector: img.findlay-testimonial__image.findlay-testimonial__image--circle Viewports: 1280×800, 1366×768, 1440×900 Fix: Add overflow:hidden to the testimonial wrapper or constrain the img max-width

Warning43 pages
WarningBROKEN_IMG — Accessibility43 pages
<img> elements with blank or missing alt attribute — separate from broken images
43 pages contain at least one <img> that loads successfully but has no alt attribute. Screen readers announce the filename or skip silently. WCAG 2.1 Level A failure (1.1.1). Use alt="" for decorative images; a meaningful description for informative ones.

8. Search Submit Button Hidden (0×0 px)

Warning116 pages
WarningFORM116 pages
button[type="submit"] inside the header search form has zero rendered dimensions
The search form's submit button has getBoundingClientRect() returning width=0, height=0 on all 116 live pages. It cannot be clicked or touched. Users can trigger search via Enter key, but mouse and touch users have no visible submit target. The 🔍 icon that opens the search panel is a separate toggle — the submit button inside the panel is the broken element.
Selector: button[type="submit"] in header search widget Fix: Remove display:none or 0-dimension override on the submit button WCAG 2.1 — 2.1.1 Keyboard, 4.1.2 Name Role Value
https://uof.rt.gw/about/ — Chrome Desktop 1366×768 — nav row 2× zoom

9. Clickable Anchor Overlap (A/A)

Warning116 pages
WarningLAYOUT116 pages
Consecutive <a> elements have intersecting bounding boxes — ambiguous click targets
The geometry check finds adjacent anchor pairs whose bounding rectangles overlap on all 116 live pages. The pattern (A/A — anchor over anchor) is consistent across every page, which points to a sitewide element as the source — most likely the overflowing nav anchors. However, since the check scans all consecutive anchors on the page (not nav-only), other stacked link pairs (footer, sidebar) may also be contributing. Root cause should be confirmed by inspecting the specific element pairs flagged.
Pattern: A/A (anchor overlapping anchor) Likely root cause: nav overflow — confirm by inspecting specific pairs Fix: Resolve nav overflow first, then re-run to identify any remaining overlaps
https://uof.rt.gw/about/ — Chrome Desktop 1366×768 — nav row 2× zoom

10. H1 or H2 Missing from DOM

Warning28 pages
WarningFONT — Heading28 pages
document.querySelector('h1') or document.querySelector('h2') returns null — incomplete heading hierarchy
28 pages in the /offices/ and /registrar/ subtrees have no <h2> element in the DOM. The H1 (page title) is present. All body content has no semantic subsection headings, which breaks the document outline for screen readers and search crawlers. All 28 pages use the same plain interior page template — a single template fix will resolve this across all of them.
Check: document.querySelector('h2') === null on 28 pages All affected pages use the /offices/ interior template Fix: Add <h2> subheadings to interior page template WCAG 2.1 — 2.4.6 Headings and Labels
